extracted.intended_audience: researchers and students in interactional sociolinguistics, pragmatics, discourse analysis, and humor studies
extracted.subtask_description: Framework for analyzing and evaluating humor as an interactional resource in everyday conversation, focusing on forms, interactional functions, and contextual conditions for success or failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multifunctionality of humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor in real conversation is a multifunctional interactional resource rather than a single-function phenomenon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete account of any humor instance must specify which functions are operative in the local context; avoid single-function reductionism (e.g., 'just relief' or 'just superiority'). The same humorous turn can simultaneously build rapport, test alignment, negotiate identity, soften face-threatening acts, establish boundaries, probe topics, release tension, and display competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canned jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-formed jokes inserted into conversation, where the teller signals a joke-frame, delivers, and returns to ordinary talk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often functions to display joke knowledge or to fill conversational space. Recognize the explicit frame shift and evaluate whether insertion and return to the prior activity are interactionally smooth or disruptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneous wit / wordplay
rubrics_metrics.description: A turn that exploits something just said for a witty effect; more integrated into ongoing talk than canned jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates quick uptake; assess timing and relevance to immediately prior talk and whether it advances alignment or displays competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anecdotes / funny stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal narratives constructed for comic effect, often serving self-presentation as much as amusement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how the storyteller uses the anecdote to present identity, solicit affiliation, or manage topic; consider sequencing and recipient design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Banter / mutual teasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal mock aggression between participants used as a relationship marker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions as evidence of closeness ('you can banter with me = we are close'). Assess reciprocity, repair moves, and whether both parties treat it as playful rather than hostile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sarcasm / irony
rubrics_metrics.description: Saying the opposite of what is meant; relies on shared contextual knowledge for the inversion to be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes shared knowledge among insiders; evaluate whether recipients have the background to detect the ironic stance and whether it risks misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-deprecation
rubrics_metrics.description: Making oneself the target of humor, with varied functions like humility, defense, bidding for sympathy, or social leveling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess intended vs. actual interpersonal effects (e.g., does it genuinely solicit sympathy or inadvertently lower status?) and how it interacts with power dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mock impoliteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate violation of politeness norms that is packaged as play rather than genuine offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions as a relationship marker; evaluate the play signals that mark it as mock (tone, framing) and whether recipients correctly treat it as non-serious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solidarity construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor used to build rapport and bond participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for inclusive positioning, shared laughter, and uptake that increases affiliation; failure occurs when humor is exclusive or alienating.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-group affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor serving as a boundary-marker that distinguishes insiders from outsiders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether shared references or knowledge are required and whether the joke reinforces group membership or excludes others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Using humor to present or negotiate what kind of person or group one is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how humor indexes traits, roles, or stances; consider how recipients interpret these identity cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power negotiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor that enacts asymmetric or symmetric power relations—asserting dominance, resisting it, or calibrating status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine who initiates, who laughs, who can safely tease whom, and how humor affects the rights and obligations in the interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politeness work
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor used to save or threaten face, or to navigate politeness norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether humor mitigates face-threatening acts, whether it masks criticism, or whether it crosses politeness boundaries; consider recipients' face concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic management
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor functioning to open, close, shift, or probe topics in conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate timing and sequence: does the humorous turn smooth a topic shift, foreclose a subject, or introduce a sensitive issue indirectly?

rubrics_metrics.name: Tension management
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor serving to dissipate awkwardness, relieve stress, or manage affective tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether humor reduces or escalates tension given the context (e.g., after bad news it may fail); inspect recipient responses for signs of relief or offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual recognition of the play frame
rubrics_metrics.description: Both parties must recognize that the turn is framed as playful/joking for the humor to function as intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for explicit or implicit play signals (intonation, smiling, markers). Failure to establish the play frame leads to misunderstanding or offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient shared background
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants need enough shared knowledge/culture for the humor to be interpretable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess shared references, cultural knowledge, or topical background; lack thereof is a common cause of joke failure across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatible interactional goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The humor's function must align with the participants' interactional aims for it to succeed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the joke's purpose (bonding, teasing, topic-probing) serves both parties; humor that conflicts with a recipient's goals may be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politeness calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: The humor must respect or skillfully exploit relevant face concerns and politeness norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the social distance, hierarchy, and context when judging appropriateness; miscalibration (e.g., too rude, too familiar) risks offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uptake (response completes the move)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient response (laugh, smile, return wit, silence) completes and ratifies the humorous move.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether uptake aligns with the intended function—lack of expected uptake indicates interactional failure; alternative uptakes can repurpose the move.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual preconditions and failure causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Situational factors (moment, relationship, power dynamic, cultural context) determine whether a structurally good joke will succeed or a weak one will work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical failure reasons: wrong interactional moment (e.g., after bad news), wrong relationship (stranger's banter reads as offense), wrong power dynamic (subordinate teasing superior), wrong cultural context. Use these as checks when evaluating success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implications for evaluating humor
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete evaluation must identify the interactional context, the functions the humor is serving, and whether the joke succeeds at those functions rather than merely judging structural form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation steps: (1) identify who, where, when, and relationship; (2) identify operative functions; (3) assess success relative to those functions (consider preconditions and uptake).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic questions for assessing conversational humor
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of guiding questions to analyze humor in interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these prompts: What forms of conversational humor are in use here? What functions is the humor serving in this interaction? Is the play frame mutually recognized? Are the interactional preconditions (relationship, context, topic timing) right? Does the uptake complete the comic move?
